tagline: Generate an llms.txt file to guide AI crawlers to your best content
pageDescription: Generate an llms.txt file with this free online generator. llms.txt is an emerging standard (llmstxt.org) that gives AI crawlers like ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity a curated, machine-friendly map of your site's most important pages. Fill in your project name, a short summary and a few sections of links, and get clean, valid Markdown to drop at the root of your domain. Everything runs in your browser with no signup. Ideal for boosting how large language models discover, understand and cite your content.

instructions.title: How to create an llms.txt file

steps.title: Name your project
steps.description: Enter your site or project name. It becomes the H1 heading at the top of the file.

steps.title: Add a summary
steps.description: Write one dense sentence describing what your site offers. It's rendered as a blockquote for the model to read first.

steps.title: Group links into sections
steps.description: Create sections like Docs, Guides or Optional, then add the key URLs with a short title and optional note for each.

steps.title: Review the output
steps.description: The valid Markdown updates live as you type, so you can see exactly what crawlers will receive.

steps.title: Download llms.txt
steps.description: Download the file and place it at the root of your domain (e.g. example.com/llms.txt).

proTips: Keep the summary information-dense — it's the first thing the model reads
Put the most important links in the first section
Use an 'Optional' section for pages LLMs can safely skip
Link to clean, content-rich pages, not navigation-heavy ones
Place the file at your domain root: example.com/llms.txt
Consider a longer llms-full.txt for complete documentation dumps
troubleshooting: Output is just the title: add at least one section with a valid link
A link is missing: both a title and a URL are required for each link
Section not showing: give it a title and at least one complete link
Crawlers ignore it: make sure the file is reachable at /llms.txt
URLs look wrong: use full absolute URLs starting with https://
